grading_system.evidence: MAUHS requires 24 credits for graduation. Course requirements for graduation meet local and state standards.

schedule.evidence: Students in grades 9-12 are required to take a full daily schedule of classes each semester. Courses run in 67-minute long blocks and 47-minute short blocks; the number of blocks per day is not stated, so courses_per_term is null.

credit_definition.text: Credit per course is not stated as a single value. The catalog gives 0.5 credit for a special-education short block and 1 whole credit for a whole block in an IEP case. Dual enrollment college courses are converted (3-credit college course = 1.0 HS credit; 1-credit = 0.25; 2-credit = 0.5).
credit_definition.evidence: the student shall earn an equivalent of 1 whole credit for the whole block

course_load.min_courses_or_credits: full daily schedule each semester (number of courses not stated); honor roll requires at least 2 credits per semester
course_load.evidence: Students in grades 9-12 are required to take a full daily schedule of classes each semester.

local_grad_requirements.conversion_note: Catalog says 'MAUHS requires 24 credits for graduation' and lists area credits: English 4, Global Citizenship 3, Math 3, Science 3 (1 Life, 1 Physical), PE 1.5, Health 0.5, Art 1, Technology 0.5, Other electives 6.5, plus Class of 2029 Civics/Financial Literacy 1. The catalog does not define 1 credit as a full-year course, so total_in_credits is null. Class of 2029 requires Civics/Financial Literacy 1 credit (Civics & Government .5 and Financial Literacy .5). Students must also meet proficiency-based graduation requirements (Vermont EQS).

flexible_pathways_listed: Advanced Placement (AP) courses, including AP through VHS
notes: Catalog is the 2026-27 course guide (Mount Anthony Union High School, Bennington). Beginning with the Class of 2024 graduation is proficiency-based under Act 77 (p.4); the catalog gives no proficiency scale. Some Southwest Tech programs have embedded graduation credits (p.4). Promotion minimums: 5 credits to grade 10, 11 to grade 11, 18 to grade 12, and 24 to graduate (p.4). Honor roll for grades 9-11 requires a full daily schedule with at least 2 credits per semester of MAU classes (p.10). Students taking college courses must be enrolled in at least two long block courses to qualify for honor roll (p.14). Dual enrollment: most college courses are 3 credits and awarded 1 high school credit (p.13). Class of 2020 completion of Personalized Learning Plan (4 years) is printed in the requirements list (p.4).
